text:
Glenn Gawdin scored his first NHL goal in the second period and added a second 3:10 later, part of a four-goal burst that turned a 1-1 game into a 5-1 Rangers win and left the Canucks winless in seven (0-7-0). Gawdin was drafted 116th overall by the Blues in 2015 and had last played in the AHL, with Stockton in 2019-20. Brock Boeser reached 500 career points on Elias Pettersson's opening goal, a moment VAN could not build on.

The scoreboard flatters the Rangers a little, and it also undersells them. Vancouver attempted 65 shots to New York's 52, and the third period belonged to the Canucks. Even so, our numbers say the Rangers were the better team. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count, favored NYR 4.51 to 2.87, and the second period was the gap: 1.90 to 0.45. Our "deserved to win" figure, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, gave NYR 74 percent. The Rangers also got a power-play goal from Oliver Bjorkstrand on their only conversion in two chances, while VAN went 0 for 4.

Dylan Garand did the rest. He stopped 27 of 28 shots and saved 1.87 goals more than the chances he faced would typically allow, a stat called goals saved above expected. He was drafted 103rd overall by the Rangers in 2020. Leevi Meriläinen allowed five on a night when the chances against him called for about 4.5. New York gets a win built on defense and goaltending, while Vancouver takes its seven-game winless run into the next one.
